newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins lower in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins lower in thin trade.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds were quoted lower compared with late Tuesday but dealers said few deals were struck, with prices edging up on fresh U.S. data which lessened market fears of another U.S. rate hike.
The U.S. Labor Department said on Wednesday the Producer Price Index (PPI) fell 0.6 percent in April. Economists had expected overall PPI to stay unchanged.
Like other emerging debt, MinFins are sensitive to any news which would suggest a further rise in U.S. interest rates, as this would push down U.S. Treasury bond prices.
On May 20 the U.S. policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee meets and could raise U.S. interest rates.
"The market was weaker in the morning and firmed after PPI. But the rise was short. Otherwise, trading was calm," one dealer said.

Dealers said the news the Paris Club hoped to reach agreement by next month paving the way for Russia's entry to the creditor nations grouping was generally positive but failed to have any impact on a market awaiting the May 20 FOMC meeting.
Nor did it react to news Russia had paid the annual three percent interest on MinFins, totalling $333.63 million.
"Nobody doubted it, so nothing happened," one dealer said.
